facts.statement: The genus Libonectes was established by Carpenter in 1997.
Libonectes morgani was originally described as Elasmosaurus morgani by Welles in 1949.
facts.quote: synonyms: Elasmosaurus morgani Welles, 1949 Libonectes atlasense Buchy, 2005

facts.statement: Libonectes atlasense was named in 2005 but is now considered a synonym of L. morgani.
facts.quote: synonyms: Elasmosaurus morgani Welles, 1949 Libonectes atlasense Buchy, 2005

facts.statement: Libonectes fossils are found in the Britton Formation of Texas and the Akrabou Formation of Morocco from the lower Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It is known from specimens found in the Britton Formation of Texas (USA) and the Akrabou Formation of Morocco, which have been dated to the lower Turonian stage of the late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The name Libonectes means 'southern swimmer' because many specimens were found in southern North America.
facts.quote: Libonectes was an elasmosaurid plesiosaur, with many specimens unearthed in southern parts of North America- as a result, it was labeled with such a name as described in the preceding sentence.

facts.statement: The species name 'morgani' honors Charles Gill Morgan, who acquired the first fossils found by T.W. Tidwell in the late 1930s.
facts.quote: Charles Gill Morgan is credited with the acquiring and preparation of the first Libonectes fossils, found by tenant farmer T.W. Tidwell in the late 1930s, and it was for this reason that morgani was chosen as the specific name part of its binomial name.

facts.statement: The complete specimen of Libonectes measured 7.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Libonectes was a medium-sized plesiosaur, with the complete specimen (SMNK-PAL 3978) measuring 7.2 m long.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Libonectes had a neck measuring 5.06 meters long.
facts.quote: The type specimen belonged to an individual with a neck measuring 5.06 m long.

facts.statement: Libonectes had taller neural spines and longer supporting processes on its neck vertebrae compared to Thalassomedon.
facts.quote: The animal was very similar to the related Thalassomedon, though the structure of the neck vertebrae was different, with taller neural spines and longer supporting processes of the bone, and its nostrils were slightly closer to the tip of the skull.

facts.statement: The type specimen of L. morgani contains the best-preserved elasmosaurid skull known.
facts.quote: The type specimen of L. morgani contains the best preserved elasmosaurid skull known as well as gastroliths.

facts.statement: While its teeth suggest a carnivorous diet, gastroliths found in fossils suggest Libonectes may have been omnivorous.
facts.quote: The possible carnivorous nature of Libonectes is suggested by its dental layout, however, the presence of gastroliths inside some known fossils feasibly indicates an omnivorous lifestyle (though paleontological investigation notes that plesiosaurs may have used gastroliths in buoyancy control).

facts.statement: Libonectes likely hunted in deep waters for small fish and ammonites due to its large size preventing it from entering shallow waters.
facts.quote: Libonectes most likely hunted in deep waters, perhaps eating small fish and ammonites, as it is thought that its bulk prevented the creature from frequenting shallow waters.

facts.statement: Researchers suspect Libonectes used its large size to trap prey because it was a slow swimmer.
facts.quote: This reptile is also suspected to have used its large size to trap prey, as a result of its slow swimming speed.

facts.statement: Libonectes lived between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)
